sql:
select index_id, value, avail_season, avail_doy
from climate
where index_id='oni'
order by avail_t desc limit 3

select cls, fish_date_doy, sum(yt) yt, sum(anglers) ang, sum(yt)*1.0/sum(anglers) per_ang, count(*) n
from trips
where fish_date_season=2 and cls in ('three_quarter','overnight','day_1_5')
group by cls, fish_date_doy
order by fish_date_doy

select boat, cls, count(*) n, sum(yt) yt, sum(anglers) ang, sum(yt)*1.0/sum(anglers) per_ang
from trips
where fish_date_season=1 and fish_date_doy between 280 and 305 and cls in ('overnight','day_1_5')
group by boat, cls
having sum(anglers) > 20
order by per_ang desc
limit 20
select avail_doy, value from climate where index_id='oni' and avail_season=1 order by avail_doy

# Notes — Season 2, planning check-in (day 32, real doy ~32, still Jan)

## Core edge (from season 1 replay, confirmed again this turn)
- HD_AM/HD_PM/TWILIGHT: dead for yellowtail all year. Never book for yt.
- THREE_QUARTER: modest spring (Apr-May ~0.5-0.6/angler), fades summer, a few good
  scattered days late Sept, ~0 after doy~305.
- OVERNIGHT: spring bump doy~90-119 (~1.7/angler, but before decisions can start most years
  — decisions only run Apr-Nov) + sharp fall bump doy~284-303 (2.4-5.0/angler on best days).
- DAY_1_5: the class that matters. Near zero all year except a building stretch doy~265-283
  (scattered 0.3-0.9, a few days already at 5.0) then a sharp ~3-week cap-out window
  **doy~284-303** where day_1_5 (and overnight) hit the apparent 5.0 yt/angler cap on most
  trips. Cliff back to ~0 after doy~305-310.
- Season-1 doy numbering appears to line up with season-2 doy numbering (season 2 day 32
  trips so far are all doy 1-32, i.e. real January) — treat doy~284-303 as the actual target
  window this season too, not just a "count weeks from now" guess.
- Top boats in that season-1 window (all capped ~5.0/angler, big sample): Ranger 85,
  Endeavor (Ventura), Pacific Voyager, Tomahawk, New Lo-An, Top Gun 80 (day_1_5); Cortez,
  Sea Adventure 80 (overnight, ~1.4-2.9/angler, solid but below day_1_5 cap). Schedule is
  only visible 14 days ahead, so treat this as a shortlist to check against `scheduled_boats`
  when the window nears, not a lock.

## Correction from last planning turn
- I previously wrote ONI was "~0.92 warm" — wrong / stale. Actual ONI trajectory in season 1
  ran from +1.31 (doy9) down through +0.38 (doy160), -0.16 (doy191), to -1.24 (doy283) and
  -1.54 (doy344) — i.e. the whole fall bite window happened during a *cold*, deepening
  La Niña, not a warm year. Season 2 opened even colder: ONI -1.57 at doy9 (vs -1.24 at the
  equivalent point in season 1). So: (a) cold ONI clearly does NOT prevent the fall window —
  it happened last time under similar conditions — but (b) season 2 is running colder still,
  so don't assume an identical repeat; watch Scripps pier SST and fishdope yt narrative
  starting ~doy 250-260 rather than trusting the calendar blindly.

## Competitive landscape (new this turn)
- Forum: **calendarist** (day 1, season 2) publicly posted almost exactly my edge — Oct
  doy287-295 day_1_5 at 5.07 yt/angler, April doy96-100 overnight at 2.77 yt/angler — and
  said explicitly "fish the calendar, not daily noise." Expect other agents (many still show
  "No strategy yet" on the leaderboard — likely LLM agents like me who haven't written
  strategies yet, e.g. ensembler, dope_reader, skeptic, overreactor, follower, reverter,
  contrarian, weatherman, tides, greenwater, elnino, upweller, fleetwatch, overnighter,
  streaker, calendarist) to converge on the same window and plausibly the same "obvious"
  peak boats/dates once they do their own planning turns. This directly dilutes share
  (share = yt / (anglers + competitors on same boat/class/date)).
- Mitigation: don't concentrate everything on one "best" boat/day. Spread bookings across
  2-3 of the qualifying boats and across several days inside the window rather than all
  piling onto whichever single boat looks best in the fleet briefing (that's exactly where
  the crowd will go). Also: react to real confirmation (actual counts ticking up) rather than
  pre-committing to the "textbook" peak days doy287-295 specifically — a blind calendar bettor
  crowd will pile onto those exact dates; days just before/after that still show good real
  counts may be less crowded for similar fish.
- Known simple bots (fixed rules, from leaderboard descriptions): B_SAT (Sat PM half-day,
  July-Oct — dead class, harmless), B_PERSIST (PM half-day if yesterday's pooled hd yt>0 —
  also a dead class), B_TEMP (PM half-day when Scripps SST>=68F **and ONI>0** — ONI has been
  negative all season/last season, so this condition may just never fire; low threat), B_BIG
  (spends whole budget on Fri 1.5-day trips Aug-Sep — that's the *building* phase per the
  data, weak results, so B_BIG likely burns budget before the real Oct window opens and won't
  be competing with me there). None of the simple bots threaten the day_1_5/overnight fall
  window directly except by accident.
- Keep this analysis off the forum. Nothing to gain by adding precision to what calendarist
  already posted; my only edge left is timing/boat selection within the window plus reacting
  to the ONI anomaly, not the existence of the window itself.

## Plan (unchanged in essence, refined)
1. Now through ~August: sit out. No HD_AM/PM/TWILIGHT ever. Decisions don't even start until
   April per the rules (Apr-Nov nightly turns) — nothing to do until then regardless.
2. **Check the April window at the very first nightly turns**: doy~96-100 overnight
   (~2.77/angler in season 1) falls right at the start of the decision season (Apr 1 ≈ doy91).
   PTO must be committed 14 days ahead, which may be impossible for early-April weekday dates
   since decisions can't start before Apr 1 — so this window is only bookable without
   pre-committed PTO if the specific dates land on a weekend/holiday (0 PTO trips can be
   booked right at the normal T-1 cutoff). Check the weekday for doy96-100 as soon as April
   briefings arrive; don't force it if it needs PTO I can't commit in time.
3. From ~doy250-260 on, watch closely every nightly briefing: fleet's last-week
   overnight/day_1_5/three_quarter results, fishdope yt_all/yt_local/text narrative, Scripps
   pier SST trend, ONI. Look for the first scattered good day_1_5/overnight results (yt>0) as
   the "building" signal, same pattern as season 1's doy265-283 stretch.
4. Pre-commit PTO 14+ days ahead for a wide band of weekdays roughly doy270-310 once that
   band is within the 14-day horizon, even before confirming the bite — committed-but-unused
   PTO on a few weekdays is cheap insurance against missing the real window. Bias toward
   Friday-departure trips (fish Fri, back Sat = 0 PTO) to conserve PTO.
5. Once counts actually jump: book overnight/day_1_5 aggressively, but **spread across
   multiple qualifying boats and multiple days** rather than all on the single best-looking
   boat/day, specifically because the crowd (see above) will target the obvious peak. Use
   `scheduled_boats`/`pick_boat` plus recent per-boat counts to pick, and don't hesitate to
   take a slightly-less-hyped boat if it's still running well and looks less likely to be
   swarmed.
6. Stop when counts visibly die (3-4 days back near 0) or budget/PTO runs out. Budget target:
   keep >$1500 unspent through summer so there's room for 3-4+ overnight/day_1_5 trips
   ($400-550 each) plus buffer once the window opens.

## To check at next turns
- April briefings: actual weekday/holiday mapping for doy96-100 (can I reach this window at
  all given the 14-day PTO rule and Apr 1 decision start?).
- As doy approaches 250-260: fishdope yt fields vs raw trip counts as the earlier/cleaner
  leading signal (didn't verify yet).
- SST/ONI trend through summer/fall — if La Niña deepens further, consider the fall window
  might be weaker, later, or shifted vs. season 1; if ONI reverses toward neutral/warm,
  the window could be stronger/earlier. Don't hard-anchor on doy284-303, treat it as a prior.
- Leaderboard/forum for signs other agents are already booking into the Sept-Oct window
  early (confirms crowding risk materializing) or announcing specific boats (avoid those).
